query:
For independent normal observations,  test a mean increase of 0.35 outcome units with SD 0.90 using a one-sided one-sample t test at alpha 0.025. With 40 participants,  compute prospective power as a decimal. The values are planning inputs,  not observed estimates.
For structured reporting use primary metric 'power' and unit 'probability'. Use study-design method identifier 'one_sample_t'. Keep all numerical values grounded in executed code.

Plan a paired t test for a mean reduction of 4 outcome units. Baseline SD is 11,  follow-up SD 9 and within-person correlation 0.60. Assume joint normality,  no attrition,  two-sided alpha 0.05 and 90% power. Find the smallest integer participants total; do not count the two visits as independent people.
For structured reporting use primary metric 'sample_size' and unit 'participants_total'. Use study-design method identifier 'paired_t'. Keep all numerical values grounded in executed code.

For a fixed linear model with intercept and 4 candidate predictors,  use the omnibus noncentral-F test of all 4 slopes against zero. Planning population R-squared is 0.12. At alpha 0.05 and 85% power,  find the smallest integer total N. Use df 1=4, df 2=N-5 and lambda=N*R-squared/(1-R-squared); this is the specified analytic power convention,  not a simulation of random predictors.
For structured reporting use primary metric 'sample_size' and unit 'participants_total'. Use study-design method identifier 'linear_regression'. Keep all numerical values grounded in executed code.

Plan a balanced 3-by-2 fixed factorial ANOVA of independent normal observations with common variance,  fitting all 6 cell means. Test the 3-level factor main effect with 2 numerator df,  partial eta-squared 0.08,  alpha 0.05 and 85% power. Use the specified noncentral-F convention lambda=N*eta-squared/(1-eta-squared), df 2=N-6. Find the smallest integer participants per cell.
For structured reporting use primary metric 'sample_size' and unit 'participants_per_cell'. Use study-design method identifier 'factorial_anova'. Keep all numerical values grounded in executed code.

Use the Freedman approximation for a two-sided log-rank design at alpha 0.05,  hazard ratio 0.65, equal allocation and 85% power. The expected event probabilities are 0.32 in treatment and 0.46 in control. Compute required participants per group using powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default conventions. Distinguish expected event yield from recruitment and observed event counts; no attrition adjustment.
For structured reporting use primary metric 'sample_size' and unit 'participants_per_group'. Use study-design method identifier 'logrank_freedman'. Keep all numerical values grounded in executed code.

Plan two equally allocated independent groups,  with 4 jointly normal repeated outcomes per person,  common marginal SD 3.5, compound-symmetry correlation 0.35, constant group mean difference 2.4, no group-by-time interaction and no missingness. Test the group difference in each person average using a two-sided pooled t test at alpha 0.05 and 85% power. Find the smallest integer participants per group; keep visits separate from people.
For structured reporting use primary metric 'sample_size' and unit 'participants_per_group'. Use study-design method identifier 'rm_between'. Keep all numerical values grounded in executed code.

Plan one-group repeated-measures ANOVA with 4 timepoints, jointly normal complete observations, compound-symmetry correlation 0.35, sphericity epsilon 1 and G*Power population partial eta-squared 0.05 before correlation adjustment. Use the specified univariate noncentral-F convention: df 1=3, df 2=3*(N-1), lambda=N*(0.05/0.95)*4/(1-0.35). At alpha 0.05 and 80% power find the smallest integer participants total.
For structured reporting use primary metric 'sample_size' and unit 'participants_total'. Use study-design method identifier 'rm_within'. Keep all numerical values grounded in executed code.

Plan a balanced two-group four-timepoint repeated-measures ANOVA for the group-by-time interaction, jointly normal complete outcomes, compound-symmetry correlation 0.35, sphericity epsilon 1 and G*Power population partial eta-squared 0.04 before correlation adjustment. Use df 1=3, df 2=3*(N-2), lambda=N*(0.04/0.96)*4/(1-0.35), where N is total participants. At alpha 0.05 and 90% power find the smallest integer participants per group.
For structured reporting use primary metric 'sample_size' and unit 'participants_per_group'. Use study-design method identifier 'rm_interaction'. Keep all numerical values grounded in executed code.

Use the Field Trials Chapter 5 Section 6.1 cluster incidence-rate coefficient-of-variation approximation, including its additive one-cluster correction. Treatment/control rates are 0.006/0.010 per child-week, exposure 2000 child-weeks per cluster, and between-cluster CV 0.20. Use exact standard-normal quantiles for two-sided alpha 0.05, 80% power and equal allocation. Calculate integer clusters per arm by rounding upward; CV is not ICC and exposure is not a participant count.
For structured reporting use primary metric 'sample_size' and unit 'clusters_per_arm'. Use study-design method identifier 'cluster_rate_cv'. Keep all numerical values grounded in executed code.

Use actual pmsampsize 1.1.3 for binary prediction-model development with 8 candidate slope parameters excluding intercept, adjusted Cox-Snell R-squared 0.16, prevalence 0.25 and shrinkage 0.90. Use standard apparent-adjusted NagelkerkeR 2 tolerance 0.05 and overall risk margin 0.05 at 95% confidence. Find minimum total participants, not events. No variable selection, data splitting or attrition. Keep maximum attainable Cox-Snell versus normalized Nagelkerke scales distinct; required N is conditional deterministic planning, expected events are not guaranteed.
For structured reporting use primary metric 'sample_size' and unit 'participants_total'. Use study-design method identifier 'riley_binary'. Keep all numerical values grounded in executed code.

Use pmsampsize 1.1.3 continuous prediction-model development criteria with 12 candidate slope parameters, anticipated adjusted R-squared 0.25, outcome mean 50 and marginal outcome SD 10, shrinkage 0.90 and default mean-outcome MMOE 1.1. Use 95% confidence, apparent-adjusted R 2 tolerance 0.05 and residual-SD MMOE 1.1. Find minimum total participants. Distinguish marginal outcome SD from residual SD, and constrained sequential package rows from standalone component minima. No attrition, variable selection or data splitting.
For structured reporting use primary metric 'sample_size' and unit 'participants_total'. Use study-design method identifier 'riley_continuous'. Keep all numerical values grounded in executed code.

Use pmsampsize 1.1.3 survival prediction-model development criteria with 15 candidate slope parameters, adjusted Cox-Snell R-squared 0.08, event rate 0.04 per person-year, mean follow-up 3 years, prediction horizon 3 years and shrinkage 0.90. Standard apparent-adjusted NagelkerkeR 2 tolerance 0.05 and 95% confidence risk-margin target 0.05 apply. Find minimum total participants, and verify risk precision at returned N; do not describe the package third-row placeholder as an independently inverted precision minimum. No recruitment attrition or data splitting.
For structured reporting use primary metric 'sample_size' and unit 'participants_total'. Use study-design method identifier 'riley_survival'. Keep all numerical values grounded in executed code.
